result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers commit to (c) and explain it well. B ties the choice more directly to how the four settings interact, such as a height range that can't be met under the chosen wind limit. B is also stronger on the no-data problem: it proposes releasing behind a flag to a slice of new users and explains how to read the metrics. It also says what to do with the rejected options: drop the video and turn the carousel into help screens at each setting. A has a stronger risk section, including what happens if the live conditions feed is down and how to handle a preview that shows 0 alerts. But A only tracks metrics without a comparison group, and it treats the carousel only as a fallback. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers commit to (c) and argue for it well. A ties its case more closely to how the settings interact, suggests a flagged rollout to a slice of new users so (c) can be compared with the current setup, and repurposes the carousel as help at each setting. B gives a stronger account of the risks, including the conditions feed failing during onboarding and a preview showing 0 alerts, but it does less to test the choice and to reuse the rejected material.
